chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: Learning positions, reading and a first taste of arranging
summary: A pianist-bandleader wrote slide positions over the notes to teach him to read; being fired suddenly stranded him and pushed him to write his own parts.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: in the middle somewhere sometimes, you know, as some pieces do. Yeah, a lot of pieces...
Yeah, when you go to a different key in...
I mean, 'It's Sand Man' has a...
Yeah, that goes into another thing in the middle, in the channel.
So you found out all those things for yourself.
So in a way, you have your own technique on the horn.

Well, there was a guy that helped me out, though. He was a piano player, I worked for him, but I finally got fired from his band. But he showed me how to read. He put a position over the note, so I... You know, I knew the positions. So he put a position over the note, and I could play it because I could see how far apart the note was, you know, above the scale or however. So I knew just what (the) sound would come out. You understand?

So that way...I guess that halfway(?) / eventually(?) helped me to learn to read. Then I started doing it, writing(?) it off like that myself, on numbered... On pieces, I'd put the position, third, fourth or second... I would put a position, you know, over the note. So that way I... I think that's a good way to teach somebody, really.
When did you first start doing some arranging?

After I got fired. I got fired without any boom, notice. Just (?), (?) that's it(?), you know. And it was the only reason because I couldn't read fast, you know. I couldn't read hardly, and you know, I had to do all the numbers like that. So they fired me with just about no kind of notice at all.
